title: When you land
body:
The realistic gateway is Phoenix Sky Harbor (PHX) — Sedona has no meaningful commercial airport of its own. From PHX it's ≈116 miles / about 2 hours by car via I-17 and AZ-179 (add 30 minutes for weekend/holiday traffic). Pick up a rental car at PHX rather than relying on rideshare once you're in Sedona (see Transit). If you'd rather not drive the mountain road yourself, a door-to-door airport shuttle (Groome Transportation and others) runs {{fact:when-you-land-55}}–100 per person, taking ≈2h45m. Flagstaff Pulliam is a smaller, closer alternative (≈30 min to Sedona) if it happens to serve your home airport — check before assuming PHX is your only option.

Budget this whole first day as travel — arriving in Sedona tired from a flight-plus-drive is normal, not a sign anything went wrong.

title: Local essentials
body: English is the primary language. Same electrical plugs and voltage as anywhere else in the US — no adapter needed. Driving is on the right. Tipping follows standard US norms: 18–20% at sit-down restaurants, $1–2/bag for hotel bellhops, $5–10/day for housekeeping (⚠ these figures move year to year and vary by property — confirm current norms before you go). Sedona sits at about 4,350 ft elevation — noticeably higher and drier than most US cities; mild altitude effects (thirst, fatigue) are common for the first day or two.

title: Entry & documents
body: This is a domestic US destination — Arizona is a US state, so a US citizen needs no passport or visa. At the TSA checkpoint for the flight itself: a REAL ID–compliant driver's license or another TSA-accepted photo ID (a US passport always works as a substitute). Without an acceptable ID, TSA's ConfirmID process costs {{fact:entry-documents-45}} as of 1 Feb 2026. ⚠ If flying in from outside the US, entry rules depend on your own passport's visa status for the United States generally — this guide's intake left home country blank, so that check wasn't done here.

title: Phone & data
body: Sedona runs on the same major US carriers as the rest of the country — if your plan covers domestic US roaming, it works here with no changes. Coverage is solid in town and along the main highways; it thins out in the canyons and at the more remote trailheads.

title: Booking checklist
body: Sedona lodging runs on the pricier side for a US destination (see Budget below) — book early, and confirm AC even though this is high desert, not tropical, since September afternoons still reach the high 80s°F.
checklist: Flights into PHX (or Flagstaff, if it serves your route)
Rental car — book ahead, prices rise closer to the date
Spa appointment (Day 2) — call L'Auberge or check Mii amo's package availability

checklist.text: Red Rock Pass — buy the 7-day pass online or at a visitor center before your first trailhead stop
checklist.note: the first trailhead day is Fri Sep 4 (Bell Rock Pathway) — this is that day, not an invented cutoff
